tale_bees_tell.name: Telling the Bees
tale_bees_tell.description: Mr Coram kept bees at {place:tale_bees} and died on Friday. Miss Hanney, who kept them with him, says somebody must knock on each of his three hives and tell them, or they'll leave. She says it ought to be family, and there isn't any.
tale_bees_tell.completion: I told them, hive by hive. The hum didn't change. One of them had comb cut from it, cleanly, the way it's done.
tale_bees_tell.returnTo: Miss Hanney, in the yard at {place:tale_bees}

requirements.text: Knock on the three hives at {place:tale_bees} and tell them

tale_bees_comb.name: Who Cuts the Comb
tale_bees_comb.description: Somebody has been cutting comb from Mr Coram's hives at {place:tale_bees} since he died, the way he did it. Miss Hanney has heard nobody, and she doesn't sleep. She asked me to wait by the hives after the bell and see who comes.
tale_bees_comb.completion: A man in a bee veil among the hives after the bell, cutting comb without a light. He said it wanted doing before the frost, and that they know him.
tale_bees_comb.returnTo: Miss Hanney, in the yard at {place:tale_bees}, by day

requirements.text: Whoever cuts the comb at {place:tale_bees}, after the bell

tale_bees_crepe.name: Black Crepe
tale_bees_crepe.description: Miss Hanney gave me black crepe to tie round Mr Coram's three hives at {place:tale_bees}. That tells the bees for certain, she said, and him. She said it's my choice, since I'm the one who saw him.
tale_bees_crepe.completion: Three hives in black crepe. Miss Hanney stood in the yard a long while, and then asked if I took sugar.
tale_bees_crepe.returnTo: Miss Hanney, in the yard at {place:tale_bees}

requirements.text: Black crepe round the three hives at {place:tale_bees}

tale_walk_follow.name: The Bell on His Ankle
tale_walk_follow.description: Mrs Pollard, at {place:tale_walk}, says her husband walks in his sleep after the bell, most nights. She ties a little bell to his ankle so that she hears him go. She asked me to follow him tonight and see where he goes.
tale_walk_follow.completion: He walked north from the house to a flat stone and set down a dinner under a cloth. He wasn't asleep. He said it was for their Tom, who is up at the School.

requirements.text: Where Mr Pollard walks to from {place:tale_walk}, after the bell

tale_walk_plate.name: The Plate
tale_walk_plate.description: Mrs Pollard wants her good plate back off the flat stone north of {place:tale_walk}, where her husband leaves a dinner every night. If there's no plate, she says, he'll stop going. She didn't say what she'll tell him.
tale_walk_plate.completion: Her good plate, off the stone, wiped clean. She put it away in the dresser and didn't say anything.

requirements.text: Mrs Pollard's plate, off the stone north of {place:tale_walk}

tale_horace_find.name: Horace
tale_horace_find.description: Mr Pargeter, at {place:tale_horace}, has lost Horace, the tortoise he had off his father. He was out of his box this morning. Mr Pargeter says to follow the bitten dandelions: Horace eats as he goes, and doesn't go fast.
tale_horace_find.completion: Horace, at the end of the bitten dandelions, facing north. He kept his head out and turned it north the whole way back.

requirements.text: Horace, at the end of the bitten dandelions by {place:tale_horace}

tale_horace_box.name: The Front of the Box
tale_horace_box.description: Horace gets out of his box at {place:tale_horace} by pushing past the front of it. Mr Pargeter wants the flat stone beside it pushed up against the front, by day, while he holds Horace. It won't stop him for good, he said. It stops him for a winter.
tale_horace_box.completion: The flat stone against the front of the box, and Horace behind it with his nose to the stone.

requirements.text: The flat stone against Horace's box at {place:tale_horace}

tale_wall_stones.name: Three Stones
tale_wall_stones.description: Mr Coker is building a dry-stone wall out from {place:tale_wall}, and his back won't lift what it did. He wants three stones carried from his heap to the end of the wall, by day, and set in the gap there. Flat and square, he said, and they go in easy.
tale_wall_stones.completion: Three dressed stones in the gap at the end of his wall. Face down they were only stone. He said they were headstones, and that nobody was using them.

requirements.text: Three stones carried to the end of {place:tale_wall}

tale_boards_back.name: The Back Window
tale_boards_back.description: Mr Rook has boarded up {place:tale_boards} with his daughter inside. He says she was out after the bell on Sunday and came back wrong. He hasn't slept since. He asked me to check that the boards over the back window are holding.
tale_boards_back.completion: The boards over the back window hold. Every nail has been worked half out, from the inside, all of them the same amount.

requirements.text: The boards over the back window at {place:tale_boards}

tale_boards_door.name: Her Side of It
tale_boards_door.description: Mr Rook won't have anybody knock at {place:tale_boards}. He sleeps after the bell, when he can. His daughter Mary is on the other side of the boards, and nobody has asked her anything.
tale_boards_door.completion: Mary Rook, through the boards, after the bell. She said her father came in on Sunday without his boots, and hasn't put them on since, because they don't fit him now.

requirements.text: Mary Rook, through the boards at {place:tale_boards}, after the bell

tale_diver_spanner.name: The Spanner
tale_diver_spanner.description: Mr Denholm, the Company's diver at {place:tale_diver}, wants the spanner out of his tool chest, which is locked. He keeps the key under the flat stone by the step, and in the suit he can't bend to it.
tale_diver_spanner.completion: The key under the stone, the spanner in the chest, and a Company chit under the spanner, folded soft. He didn't ask for the chit.

requirements.text: The key under the flat stone at {place:tale_diver}
The spanner in the tool chest at {place:tale_diver}

tale_scarf_rows.name: The Last Rows
tale_scarf_rows.description: Mrs Wakes, at {place:tale_scarf}, knits one row for everybody who comes up her path. Her eyes are going. She asked me to read her the newest rows, off the scarf where it hangs over the arm of her chair, to be sure she has everybody right.
tale_scarf_rows.completion: Names worked into the rows in a darker wool, one to a row. The last row is cast on, with no name in it yet. She said she'd have it by the time I went.

requirements.text: The newest rows of Mrs Wakes's scarf, at {place:tale_scarf}

tale_scarf_row.name: Your Row
tale_scarf_row.description: Mrs Wakes has cast on a row of her scarf for me. She can finish it or pull it out, she said, and it's my row. Finished, I'm counted. Pulled out, nobody has me down anywhere, and she wouldn't like that for anybody.
tale_scarf_row.completion: My row, decided, on the arm of her chair.

requirements.text: Your row, on the scarf over her chair at {place:tale_scarf}

tale_halt_oil.name: Lamp Oil
tale_halt_oil.description: Mr Voysey keeps {place:tale_halt}. The signal lamps are dry, and the oil is in the lamp locker. A barrel has rolled against the locker and he can't shift it. His back isn't what it was, he said.
tale_halt_oil.completion: A can of paraffin, a third full. Enough for one lamp.

requirements.text: The oil in the lamp locker at {place:tale_halt}

tale_halt_lamp.name: The Red Lamp
tale_halt_lamp.description: Mr Voysey wants the red signal lamp at {place:tale_halt} lit after the bell, so that the Sunday train runs through and doesn't stop. There's oil for one lamp. Mrs Voysey sits by the bench with her case. She says to light the green.
tale_halt_lamp.completion: One signal lamp lit at the halt, after the bell. The other stayed dark.

requirements.text: A signal lamp lit at {place:tale_halt}, after the bell

tale_vermin_clear.name: Vermin
tale_vermin_clear.description: Mr Sorrell is the Company's vermin man at {place:tale_vermin}. Web spinners have got into the walls there, more than he can see to. He's paid by the head, and he'd split it with me. Four would do.
tale_vermin_clear.completion: Four spinners down. Mr Sorrell counted them twice, and then looked at the hatch in the floor.

requirements.text: Web spinners in the walls at {place:tale_vermin}

tale_vermin_hatch.name: Under the Hatch
tale_vermin_hatch.description: Whatever is under the hatch at {place:tale_vermin} lives on the spinners that fall in, and I've killed its supper. Mr Sorrell says it comes up after the bell when it's hungry. Either something goes down the hatch first, or somebody is there when it comes up.
tale_vermin_hatch.completion: The hatch at the Weighbridge, after the bell, and whatever was under it seen to, one way or the other.

requirements.text: The hatch in the floor at {place:tale_vermin}, after the bell
